_comment: SHA-256 digests of the DER certificates Roblox signs com.roblox.client with.
This is the whole of what makes an archive from a source that is not Roblox
acceptable (ADR-025): a mirror can serve the wrong bytes, and it cannot forge
the signing key. A digest here is public information -- anyone can compute it
from any genuine Roblox APK, and `cargo run -p cordial-update --example
verify-apk -- <path>` prints it -- so this file is a convenience for auditing
It is a file rather than a constant so that a person can read it, diff it, and
change it without a release. If Roblox rotates its signing certificate every
download fails closed until a digest is added here, which is the correct
direction to fail and needs to be a one-line fix somebody can make quickly.
Adding one is a decision, not a chore: a digest added here is a key Cordial
will accept builds from forever. Take it from an APK you already trust, and
`quest_certificates` is a separate list, read only when importing a Quest build
the user pulled from their own headset (ADR-053). The Quest build is signed with
a key the phone build is not, and keeping it out of `certificates` means it
widens nothing an update or a mirror download will install.

certificates.note: Read from the base.apk Sober downloaded on this machine, and cross-checked with an independent implementation of the v2 signing-block parse before being written down.

quest_certificates.note: Read from the APK Meta's store installed on a Quest 3, pulled with `adb pull`. The v2 signature verifies to this certificate: self-signed, subject and issuer O=Roblox Corporation, CN=Roblox Corporation, valid 2023-03-31 to 2050-08-16. A self-signed subject proves nothing on its own; the provenance is the headset's store install.
